verdict.rationale: Linear documents a developer framework for building custom agent apps that work inside the product. Issues can be assigned to the app as a delegate, and agent session state is shown to users in the interface, so custom integrations do operate within Linear's own UI. The evidence covers only this agent surface, not general UI extension points; the GraphQL API alone is a building block and earns no credit. Missing for 10: documented custom UI surfaces or extension points (panels, views, embedded components) beyond agent delegation and session display, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build custom integrations that appear and operate directly inside the product's own interface

citations.quote: You can build agents for internal use within your own workspace or for distribution to other organizations.
Assigning an issue to your app now sets it as the `delegate`, not the `assignee`—so humans maintain ownership while agents act on their behalf.
Session state is visible to users, and updated automatically based on the agent’s emitted activities.
